transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

For months now I’ve had this constant heavy, sad feeling that I just can’t seem to shake, even when I’m doing things I used to enjoy. My primary care doctor noticed I wasn't quite myself during a routine check-up and recommended I come speak with you.
Have you ever experienced similar periods of deep sadness in the past, or is this the very first time you have felt this way?

This is the very first time I've ever felt this level of persistent, heavy sadness. Before these last eight months, I've always been a very active, organized person who stayed busy and engaged with my community.
Along with this heavy sadness over the past eight months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, appetite, or daily energy levels?

My sleep has been a major issue; I wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning with my mind churning and just can't fall back asleep. Because of that, I feel constantly drained and tired during the day, though my appetite hasn't really changed.
Have you found it harder to concentrate, focus, or make decisions lately, or have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt?

My concentration is mostly okay, but I am constantly overwhelmed by this heavy sense of guilt that I'm failing everyone. I feel like a lousy sister for not being there in person for my sister, a poor friend for canceling plans, and I just don't feel like I bring much value to anyone's life anymore.
During these past eight months, have you had any thoughts of harming yourself, or felt that life is no longer worth living?

I don’t have any plans to hurt myself, but on my really low days, I do think that if I just didn’t wake up in the morning it would be a relief. It feels like it would make things much simpler for everyone else around me.
Have you ever experienced periods lasting at least a few days where you felt unusually happy, highly energetic, or hyperactive, perhaps needing very little sleep?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. My energy has actually been the exact opposite—just very low and heavy for these past several months.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with an 8-month history of a first-time depressive episode. She meets criteria for a depressive episode (F32) with a persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, early morning awakening (insomnia), fatigue, excessive guilt, and passive suicidal ideation. She has no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, ruling out bipolar disorder, and this is her first episode, ruling out recurrent depressive disorder.
